candidates: When specifying special-key names for keyboard shortcuts in `ase/gui` — in `gui.py`'s dispatch dict and `M()` menu calls — use human-readable display names that render correctly in menus across all platforms (e.g., 'PageUp', 'PageDown'), not hyphenated variants ('Page-Up'/'Page-Down') nor raw Tk canonical names ('Prior'/'Next'). Tk names render as single letters in Mac menus and are displayed verbatim on Linux, both of which are unhelpful to users. The `MenuItem` class in `ui.py` owns the mapping from these human-readable names to Tk key identifiers (e.g., 'PageUp' → '<Prior>'), so any new special key must have a corresponding entry added to that mapping table to keep both layers in sync.
